note: Cases for test_contract_studio (studioOpsLikePython): the studio ops of M5 (Python's genko/studio/studio_ops.py, which ops.apply_ops dispatches its STUDIO_OPS to) and set_bible, add_ticket and set_ticket (ops._apply_one) on the book `studio_harness.py make-studiobook` makes: the op contract book (pyref_harness.py make-opsbook: page 5 held by ai:other, a front cover as page 7) with a studio — characters (c-ken's sheet approved and locked), locations, a prop, a script, a page plan, briefs (page 1: a pinned shot and a prompt override on 000000000028, a person's fix on 000000000029, regions, a reference, three candidates and the art adopted on 000000000026), requests, sheet candidates from two agents and a person, tickets of every kind, two proposals, the style fixed from page 6 — and its pictures ($A1 … $G1 PNGs, $J1 a JPEG, $CUT a PNG cut short after its header, $BAD bytes that are no picture, $CRC a PNG whose header's checksum is wrong, $BOMB a header too large to open, $JX $BX $GX a JPEG, a BMP and a GIF cut short in their pixels; refs from the book's assets.json). Each case: its steps ({ops, agent?, dry_run?}; or one step of ops, agent, dry), whether its last step succeeds in Python, with time.strftime fixed (allow_chat_approval). A case marked "cpp" is one this build refuses on purpose (a number Python makes from text, 'inf' or 'nan', that it would keep; what only a person holds, changed by an agent; a picture placed whose pixels cannot be decoded): C++ must refuse it with that code, its error holding "cpp_says".
